title: Restriction of Steinberg sections to the infinitesimal torus neighbourhood is injective
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], of prime characteristic $p>0$, and let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Semisimple means smooth, affine, connected and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, where solvable means that the successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. Simply connected means that every surjective homomorphism $S'\to S$ from a semisimple group scheme with finite central kernel is an isomorphism; finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and central means commuting with every element after every scalar extension. A split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some $r\ge0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$; a maximal torus is one not contained in a larger torus. A Borel subgroup is a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$. For this pair, let $\Phi^+$ be the positive roots given by the nonzero characters of the adjoint action of $T$ on $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, where $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$ is the kernel of $B(F[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2))\to B(F)$, with its tangent-space structure. A character is a group-scheme homomorphism $T\to\mathbf G_m$; addition of characters means multiplication of their values. Let $\rho\in X^*(T)$ satisfy $2\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$, and let $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$ extend it and be trivial on the unipotent radical of $B$; this radical is its largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, with unipotent meaning that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. Fix an integer $r\ge1$ and write $q=p^r$ and $\lambda=(q-1)\rho$. If $C=F[S]$, define $S^{(q)}=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{F,a\mapsto a^q}F)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; its group operations are obtained by this base change. The relative Frobenius $F^r_{S/F}:S\to S^{(q)}$ has coordinate map $c\otimes a\mapsto ac^q$. Let $T^{(q)}\subseteq S^{(q)}$ be the base change of $T$, let $S_r=\ker F^r_{S/F}$, and define the closed subgroup schemes $L_r=(F^r_{S/F})^{-1}(T^{(q)})$ and $P_r=B\cap L_r$, with scheme-theoretic inverse image and intersection. Use the notation $S_rT=L_r$ and $B_rT=P_r$. On $P_r$ use the restriction of the given $B$-character $\widetilde\rho$. Define the actual infinitesimal induced module
$$Z_r=\{f\in F[L_r]:f(xb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^{q-1}f(x)\text{ for every commutative }F\text{-algebra }D,\ x\in L_r(D),\ b\in P_r(D)\}.$$
Use left translation $(h f)(x)=f(h^{-1}x)$. A rational module for an affine group scheme $K$ is an $F$-vector space with a coassociative counital coaction $M\to M\otimes_FF[K]$; a submodule is an $F$-linear subspace whose coaction lands in its tensor product with $F[K]$. Equivariance means equality of coactions, equivalently equality after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Write $\widehat Z'_r(\lambda)=Z_r$ for this choice of positive roots in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$. Define also the actual section module
$$E_r=\{f\in F[S]:f(gb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^{q-1}f(g)\text{ for every commutative }F\text{-algebra }D,\ g\in S(D),\ b\in B(D)\},$$
with left translation. Restriction of regular functions along $L_r\hookrightarrow S$ induces an injective $F$-linear map $E_r\hookrightarrow Z_r$ which is equivariant for $L_r$, where the $L_r$-action on $E_r$ is restricted from its rational $S$-action. This includes the trivial group and all primes $p$, including $2$.

proof.text: Put $H_r=(F^r_{S/F})^{-1}(B^{(q)})$ and let $V_r$ be the semi-invariant functions on $H_r$ with the covariance in the question. Apply [lem-sfb-frobenius-borel-induction-geometry] with $\chi=\widetilde\rho^{-(q-1)}$: restriction $V_r\to Z_r$ is an $L_r$-equivariant isomorphism, and $\pi_q:S\to Q_q$ is the right $H_r$ quotient with $Q_q$ proper and geometrically integral. Apply [lem-sfb-steinberg-borel-thickening-extension] to equip the finite-dimensional space $V_r$ with an $S$-action extending its specified $H_r$-translation action. Both inputs use exactly the given $B,T,r$ and sign convention.

source.place: Sections 2.3--2.5, pp.320--323; explicit assembly supplied by Q89 from the extension input (2.5)(9) and quotient (2.5)(3), before Kempf

proof.text: For $f\in E_r$, define a regular $V_r$-valued function $A_f$ on $S$ by $A_f(g)(h)=f(gh)$ for $h\in H_r$. Right $B$-covariance in the variable $h$ places it in $V_r$. Regularity follows directly from multiplication: the pullback of $f$ is in $F[S]\otimes_FF[H_r]$; expand its finitely many coefficients in a linearly independent family in $F[S]$. The covariance equation puts each coefficient in $V_r$, so the pullback lies in $F[S]\otimes_FV_r$. For $a\in H_r$ one has $A_f(ga)(h)=f(gah)=(a^{-1}A_f(g))(h)$, by the left-translation convention. These are identities after every scalar extension.

source.place: Sections 2.3--2.5, pp.320--323; explicit assembly supplied by Q89 from the extension input (2.5)(9) and quotient (2.5)(3), before Kempf

proof.text: Set $C_f(g)=g\cdot A_f(g)$ using the extended action. This is regular and $C_f(ga)=ga\cdot(a^{-1}A_f(g))=C_f(g)$. The quotient property in [lem-sfb-frobenius-borel-induction-geometry] makes $C_f$ descend to $Q_q$. Choose a basis of the finite-dimensional $V_r$. Each coordinate of the descended map is in $\Gamma(Q_q,\mathcal O)$, which is $F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-reduced-algclosed-global-sections-product]: geometric integrality implies nonempty connected reduced, and properness is given in step 1. Thus $C_f$ is the constant $C_f(1)=A_f(1)=f|_{H_r}$, and $A_f(g)=g^{-1}\cdot(f|_{H_r})$.

source.place: Sections 2.3--2.5, pp.320--323; explicit assembly supplied by Q89 from the extension input (2.5)(9) and quotient (2.5)(3), before Kempf

proof.text: If $f|_{L_r}=0$, the restriction isomorphism of [lem-sfb-frobenius-borel-induction-geometry] gives $f|_{H_r}=0$. Step 3 then gives $A_f=0$, hence $f(g)=A_f(g)(1)=0$ as a regular function. This proves injectivity. Restriction is linear. For $a,x\in L_r(D)$, $((a f)|_{L_r})(x)=f(a^{-1}x)=(a(f|_{L_r}))(x)$; since this holds for every commutative $F$-algebra $D$, it proves equality of coactions and $L_r$-equivariance. For $S=1$, both spaces are $F$ and restriction is the identity; no step divided by $2$ or excluded a small prime.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q89-9248a3978 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The item statement is unchanged and true. With Lie(B) positive, E_r is Jantzen's H^0((q-1)rho)=St_r and Z_r is Ẑ'_r((q-1)rho), both after a w0 twist. New node lem-sfb-frobenius-borel-induction-geometry is true. B is smooth, so F^r is fppf surjective on B. That makes L_r×B→H_r a P_r-torsor, giving H_r/B≅L_r/P_r and the restriction isomorphism I_{H_r}(chi)≅I_{L_r}(chi) for every chi; the inverse is phi(l,b)=chi(b)^{-1}f(l). S/H_r≅S^(q)/B^(q) is the proper integral flag variety. New node lem-sfb-steinberg-borel-thickening-extension is true: the B→G_rB induced module at the Steinberg weight is St_r restricted to G_rB, and the source's sign conversion is correct. Neither new node restates the item or duplicates an existing node; I read reductive-frobenius-twist, scalar-p-isogeny, infinitesimal-induced-simple, weyl-restricted-freeness, restricted-module-infinitesimal-simplicity and restricted-frobenius-tensor-simplicity, and ran rg -L over dag/nodes. Steps: (1) chi=rho~^{-(q-1)} has the right sign. (2) A_f(g)(h)=f(gh) is regular and V_r-valued by coefficient independence, with A_f(ga)=a^{-1}A_f(g). (3) C_f=g·A_f(g) is H_r-invariant, descends to Q_q, and is constant because Γ(Q_q,O)=F by the proper-reduced global-sections lemma, so A_f(g)=g^{-1}f|_{H_r}. (4) f|_{L_r}=0 gives f|_{H_r}=0, then A_f=0, then f=0; L_r-equivariance is checked on D-points. Tests: S=1, SL2 (dimensions q=q), p=2. The closure avoids induced-module-irreducible, Kempf vanishing and the Weyl dimension formula, and has no cycle. These are generic scheme results, not steps of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proofs, and all three are already in the parent's closure, so the flag is accepted. The declared tool_use for that lemma is accepted. Kaneda and Jantzen are not in literature/ and are marked WANTED; I checked both statements mathematically instead. No fixes.
